thread:
maria: Heads up — since ~08:10 UTC we've had a spike of pod <-> pod disconnects on the shadow GPU pool in westasia (cluster: gpu-shadow-westasia). Multiple apps reporting 502s and grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.

aj: Noted. Any pattern on which pods? actors vs workers?

maria: Primarily model-workers (prefetch + inference sidecars). Restarting a few pods temporarily recovers them. Also seeing high SYN retransmits between pods.

kevin: Can you paste conntrack counts from one of the affected nodes?

maria: Sure — grabbed from gpu-node-17: 
```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count = 65536
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 65536
# conntrack -L | wc -l
65536
```

maria: So the table is full. Also saw a bunch of ESTABLISHED -> TIME_WAIT churn for ephemeral ports.

tara: Oof. That matches the pod logs we saw: a lot of outbound connections to internal model cache services with very short-lived sockets. Likely SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion.

aj: Are these nodes using host SNAT (kube-proxy iptables/ipvs) or masquerade agent from CNI?

maria: kube-proxy ipvs + weave overlay for east-west. CNI uses masquerade.

kevin: Could be a combination: overlay MTU mismatch causing packet fragmentation/loss and retransmits which blow up conntrack entries as connections get stuck. Also RDMA-enabled nodes have different path MTU when veth->ib0 is involved.

sre-bot: [alert] conntrack table full on gpu-node-17 (65536/65536) — triggered at 1967654300

maria: I pulled iptables SNAT stats: lots of counters on the SNAT chain. kubernetes services generating many translations.

aj: Quick mitigation — bump nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes to 262144 and clear stale entries. But need cluster-wide fix.

kevin: Agreed. Short-term steps (1-2hr):
- sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
- echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait (reduce TIME_WAIT?) (note: needs validation)
- conntrack -L | grep "SYN_RECV" | wc -l (identify half-open)

maria: Ran conntrack -S and saw high new and expect counts: 
```
# conntrack -S
root->nf_conntrack: used 65536 entries, found 0, new 120/s, invalid 0, ignore 0
```

tara: We should also inspect gRPC keepalive and connection reuse in model-worker client code. If they open many short connections vs reusing long ones, that will burn ephemeral ports.

kevin: Long-term: reduce SNAT pressure by enabling externalTrafficPolicy: Local for service mesh egress? Or consider implementing node-local proxy for model cache (sidecar or daemon) to multiplex connections. Also tune kube-proxy ipvs conntrack timeout and hashsize.

aj: Another vector — RDMA NICs (Mellanox) had kernel offload bugs where small retransmits were retried and created additional nat entries when falling back to TCP over veth. Are the affected nodes on the RDMA pool?

maria: Yes, gpu-node-15..19 are RDMA-enabled and part of shadowpool.

kevin: Try disabling offloads on one node as an experiment: 
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 tx off rx off gso off gro off tso off
```
If retransmits fall, then it's an offload/MTU issue. But this impacts throughput.

maria: Did a quick test on gpu-node-17: disabled gso/gro -> retransmits down 60% and conntrack entries stabilized after clearing.

aj: Good. Plan then: 1) immediate bump nf_conntrack_max + conntrack -F on nodes 15-19; 2) roll a config to disable problematic offloads for RDMA nodes (can use a daemonset to toggle ethtool); 3) follow up with kernel driver vendor and Mellanox firmware; 4) code changes to client side to reuse connections and increase keepalive.

tara: Also add proactive alerting on conntrack used% per node and ephemeral port usage per node so we catch earlier. Add a Grafana panel and an alert at 70% usage.

maria: I'll run the hotfix now. @deploy-bot can you schedule a config rollout window in the next 30m? Need a short maintenance window for the daemonset to toggle offloads.

deploy-bot: Scheduling config rollout: eng-infra maintenance window at 09:00-09:30 UTC. Will create canary rollout targeting gpu-node-15.

kevin: Also note cost implication: increasing conntrack_max increases kernel memory usage ~ (entries * 320 bytes). If we go to 262k that's ~80MB per node — acceptable. But if we need 1M entries that's O(320MB) per node. Keep an eye on node memory.

aj: For fleet capacity: this pattern can inflate perceived pod failures and lead to autoscaler churn (more pods spun up, more connections, more pressure). So fixing connection reuse reduces both latency and cost.

maria: Hotfix applied on gpu-node-15 as canary: 
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
conntrack -F
```
Post-fix: conntrack used -> 46000, retransmits dropped, model-workers recovered.

tara: Nice. Can we add a temporary iptables rule to ACCEPT RELATED,ESTABLISHED faster?

kevin: iptables order matters but conntrack still has to store state. Accepting earlier helps CPU but not table size. Focus on reducing connections.

maria: I'll open a follow-up ticket with action items:
- permanent sysctl change via node-config for RDMA pool
- daemonset to disable offloads on affected NICs (with rollback)
- app work: connection pooling + keepalive tuning for model cache clients
- alerting dashboard for conntrack usage and ephemeral port exhaustion
- vendor escalation with Mellanox on offload/firmware weirdness

aj: LGTM. One more: consider configuring NAT46/Proxy for service-to-service on same node (hostNetwork) for hot paths so we skip SNAT entirely.

maria: Good call. I'll add that to the ticket.

sre-bot: [resolved] conntrack saturation on gpu-node-17 — mitigation applied (1967654560) :white_check_mark:

kevin: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short postmortem + cost impact estimate tomorrow.

maria: Thanks all — leaving the thread here. :thumbsup:
